dossiers.droits-de-douane.sections.4.tit: The American case: from “Liberation Day” to today
dossiers.droits-de-douane.sections.4.par: On 2 April 2025, Donald Trump announced from the White House Rose Garden what he called “Liberation Day”: a 10% tax on almost everything entering the United States from 5 April, then higher rates country by country, for example 34% for China, 20% for the European Union, 24% for Japan and 46% for Vietnam [6]. These rates were calculated mainly from the US trade deficit with each country, not from the taxes those countries applied themselves [6].

Revenue rose sharply. The federal government collected $195 billion in customs duties in fiscal year 2025 (October 2024 to September 2025), then $173 billion in fiscal 2026, an 11% drop mainly due to refunds [7]. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) expects about $250 billion less for 2026 than in its earlier projections [8].

Why refunds? On 20 February 2026, the Supreme Court ruled 6–3 that the emergency economic powers law (IEEPA) used for these taxes did not give the president the power to create tariffs [9]. The same day, the White House replaced them with a temporary 10% surcharge for 150 days, which ended on 24 July 2026, then with new taxes of 10% to 12.5% on about sixty countries, based on another law [9][10].

Who pays? According to Yale University's Budget Lab, the tariffs in place cost the typical American household more than $1,000 a year (August 2026 estimate) [11]. Well-off households pay more in dollars, but low-income households pay more as a share of their income [12].

Where does the money go? Customs duties go into the government's general budget, with no separate fund. On 8 December 2025, the government announced $12 billion in aid for farmers hit by the trade war, funded, according to the president, by “a small portion” of tariff revenue [13]. On the other hand, the $2,000-per-person “tariff dividend” promised on 9 November 2025 was never passed: it would have cost about $300 billion according to the Tax Foundation [14].
